plants.subsector: Electrical Equipment, Appliance, and Component Manufacturing

plants.note: The Austin American-Statesman (4 Feb 2026, read in Yahoo's copy): Base Power 'moved into the former Austin American-Statesman waterfront building at 305 S. Congress Ave. in October of last year' as 'a temporary factory', and 'has operated manufacturing and shipping from the site'. Solar Power World (5 Aug 2026): 'already producing thousands of Base Core units a month in Austin'. The site is slated for redevelopment, so this factory is temporary by the company's own account. The Census geocoder puts the address 250 m west on the street (30.25806, -97.74646); the Esri address point is the building. plants.note: State registration TABS2026013248 ('Base Power Met 3 Phase 1', registered 23 Feb 2026): tenant finish-out of a shell building, 'Includes manufacturing and warehouse uses', 216,060 sq ft, scheduled 11 May to 11 Dec 2026. The dates are the registration's schedule; no source read says the factory has opened, so it is written as under construction. The coordinate is the address point for 8001 Metropolis Dr, a campus of several buildings; Building 3 itself was not located.

notes.houston:
WHAT THIS FILE IS. Factories of the Houston (Houston-Pasadena-The Woodlands metro area: Harris, Fort Bend, Montgomery, Brazoria, Galveston, Chambers, Liberty, Waller and Austin counties) and Beaumont-Port Arthur (Jefferson, Orange, Hardin) hubs that the seven earlier research files miss or describe without people, measured against a migrated copy of production on 2026-11-24 into which the seven files had been reloaded (the copy had their rows without their facts). Largest by people first. Evadale (Jasper County) is included because it is the Beaumont area's paper mill.

HOW FACTS WERE GOT. Headcounts are the 'annual average number of employees' each establishment reported to OSHA on Form 300A for 2025 (2024 where there is no 2025 row), read from the copies of OSHA's establishment files already on disk from the earlier research (osha.gov itself was not asked). The figure is the employer's own people at that address, offices on the site included, contractors not included; each employeesNote names the filed establishment. Hours worked were checked against each figure; where they do not fit, the note says so. Products are one line from the industry the establishment filed (its NAICS description), sharpened only where a page read says more (PV Hardware, Mahindra, Methanex, Plug Power, Intuitive Machines, Axiom Space, Venus Aerospace, Solugen, Syzygy). opened is given only where a page states it (Intuitive Machines 2023, PV Hardware 2024).

COORDINATES. US Census Bureau geocoder (batch and single), exact house-number match, where it gave one; otherwise the ArcGIS World Geocoding Service, accepted only when its answer was a PointAddress or StreetAddress with the same house number and street (SLB Katy, SLB Bits, Dessert Holdings, Buckhead Meat & Seafood, TPC Group, MOGAS, TAS Energy Robin Street, Jindal Saw, Dover Pearland, Ball Conroe, SUHM, Crown Sugar Land, Solugen, Builders FirstSource Beltway, Starplast, Buckeye Corrugated, Emerson Jersey Village, Dow Bayport, Riviana, Arlanxeo, Biotics, Cameron Houston, Methanex, Baker Hughes Deer Park, Crown Conroe, Conrad Orange, Syzygy). ArcGIS's terms for storing results without a key are the owner's call; every such point is listed in notes.md. The filled plants keep the earlier files' coordinates.

FILLED, NOT NEW. Dow Deer Park Operations, Frito-Lay Rosenberg, Celanese Clear Lake, Smurfit Westrock Evadale and JSW Steel USA Baytown are copied from their earlier files with the newer OSHA figure; every other field is as those files have it, so a second load keeps the newer headcount and changes nothing else.

DOUBTS. Syzygy Plasmonics' site is described by the National Association of Manufacturers as an industrial demonstration plant, and the OSHA filing calls it Pearland at a Houston address. Axiom Space's 600 Gemini Street filing is its headquarters; KPRC says the suits are built in Houston without naming the building. Plug Power's Houston site also repairs cryogenic equipment. notes.dfw: WHAT THIS FILE IS. Dallas-Fort Worth (the 11 counties of the Dallas-Fort Worth-Arlington metro area) and Sherman-Denison (Grayson County), with two sites just outside them (Mineral Wells, Palo Pinto County). Factories the earlier Texas files did not carry, and one fact filled on a factory they do (Bell Fort Worth (Plant 1): opened 1952). Built on 2026-11-24 after measuring a copy of production with every earlier research file replayed onto it: 1,783 factories in the two metro areas, 149 with a headcount. HEADCOUNTS come from OSHA's establishment files (Form 300A, https://www.osha.gov/Establishment-Specific-Injury-and-Illness-Data), read from the copies already on disk from the 2026-11-18 download; nothing was asked of osha.gov. The figure is the establishment's own annual average number of employees at that address for 2025, or for 2024 when there is no 2025 filing (the note says so); offices on the site are included, contractors are not. WHICH: every manufacturing establishment (NAICS 31 to 33) in the two metro areas that filed 150 or more people, is a factory, and is not already in a research file, chosen by hand; below 150 only those picked for a reason (a known employer, a new or growing company); plus the plants the earlier OSHA brief left unplaced in this area (US Conec, Taylor Farms Texas, Sterilite, Freshpet, Petmate, MSI Express, Parker Filtration Mineral Wells) and two it left in doubt that sources settle (Shield AI's V-BAT building, Qorvo's Campbell Road site). Emerging and new factories added from company pages and news: MP Materials (Fort Worth magnets, 2024), Foxlink (Fort Worth circuit board assembly, opened July 2026), LiquidStack (Carrollton data-center cooling, 2023), GD-OTS Mesquite (155 mm projectile metal parts, 2024), Repkon USA (bought GD-OTS Garland in 2025), Louis Vuitton's Rochambeau Ranch workshop (2019), Aspire MRO and Mammoth Freighters (777 freighter conversions at Alliance), Shield AI (V-BAT, 2023). COORDINATES: the US Census geocoder's answer for the filed street address, accepted only when its house number, street name and street direction agree with the filing (a match on the other side of a street direction was refused: 1001 N Cockrell Hill answered as S Cockrell Hill, 803 W Carrier answered as N Carrier); otherwise the EPA registry's point for a facility at the same address (ECHO Exporter, published 2026-11-15, read from disk; the plant's sources then carry its detailed facility report). Five were placed by hand at the registry's point (ATCO on ATCO Drive, Carolina Beverage at 13300 Park Vista, UFP Grandview on Highway 81, Taylor Farms at 1001 N Cockrell Hill, MSI Express at 803 W Carrier Pkwy); Louis Vuitton is at the Census answer for 5500 County Road 316. Seven could not be placed and are in unplaced. PRODUCTS are one plain line from the filing's industry and the company's own description; treat them as descriptions. COMPANIES: a company already in another research file keeps that file's name, domain and parent. A domain is given only where the company's own site was reached or is well known; 'alsoKnownAs' are the exact names the rehearsal found rows stored under. GROUPING CALLS: ATCO Rubber Products under parent Mueller Industries (the filing names Mueller); Pottorff under parent PCI Industries (the filing names PCI); Meyer Utility Structures under parent Arcosa; Teledyne Micropac under Teledyne; Presto Products under Reynolds Consumer Products; Fresh Express under Chiquita; TurboChef under Middleby; EF Johnson under JVCKenwood; Owen Oil Tools under Core Laboratories; Progress Rail under Caterpillar; Heritage Bag under Novolex; BrassCraft under Masco; Whitmore under CSW Industrials; Continental Electronics under OSI Systems. The rehearsal on the copy of production (load texas-dfw) found 65 of the 124 companies and created 59; the corrections file in this folder names seven rows that are these factories under a former owner's name. LEFT OUT: repair and overhaul sites (StandardAero Dallas Airmotive, Pratt & Whitney Grand Prairie, Gulfstream Dallas and Alliance, Trinity Rail Maintenance, MTU Fort Worth), offices and engineering campuses filing a manufacturing code (Collins Aerospace Richardson, CAE Arlington, Raytheon Plano and Expressway, Motorola Allen and Dallas, Analog Devices Dallas, STMicroelectronics Coppell, Boeing Richardson, Crestron Plano, Delta Electronics Plano, Applied Materials Richardson), distribution and fulfilment (Amazon, Carvana, HelloFresh, Coca-Cola Southwest's distribution centers, Frito-Lay's service center), ready-mix, precast and asphalt (NAICS 32732, 32733, 32739, 324121), and those whose site or product could not be told from the filing (Standard Motor Products Lewisville, Salcomp Arlington, Jabil Richardson, OmniOn Plano, Honeywell Richardson, Peterbilt's 1700 Woodbrook St, Kroger's Irving beverage plant code 256-PL002, True Velocity Garland on a 2024 filing only, Koya Medical, axium solar).

notes.rest:
WHAT THIS FILE IS. Factories of the rest of Texas that the seven earlier research files miss, describe without people, or describe with a figure years old: the metro areas of El Paso, Corpus Christi, Victoria, College Station-Bryan, Tyler, Longview, Lubbock, Amarillo, Midland, Odessa, Abilene and Wichita Falls (with the towns next to them: Calhoun County, Navasota, Brenham, Athens, Jacksonville, Borger, Pampa, Big Spring, Sweetwater and Snyder, Olney and Vernon), and the largest factories elsewhere in Texas outside the Austin, Dallas-Fort Worth, Houston-Beaumont and San Antonio-Valley-Laredo briefs (the Rio Grande Valley, Laredo and the border towns are that brief's and are left to it). Measured against a migrated copy of production on 2026-11-24 into which the seven files had been reloaded (the copy had their rows without their facts). Largest by people first.

HOW FACTS WERE GOT. Headcounts are the 'annual average number of employees' each establishment reported to OSHA on Form 300A for 2025 (2024 where there is no usable 2025 row), read from the copies of OSHA's establishment files already on disk from the earlier research (osha.gov itself was not asked). The figure is the employer's own people at that address, offices on the site included, contractors not included; each employeesNote names the filed establishment. A figure is written only when the hours reported give 1,000 to 3,000 hours a person; otherwise the plant carries oshaNotWritten and no headcount. The Pantex Plant files no Form 300A; its figure is the plant's own page. Products are one line from the industry the establishment filed (its NAICS description), sharpened only where a page read says more (Cheniere, Tesla's refinery, Pantex, AST SpaceMobile, BioVeritas, Skeeter, Tige, Novipax, Handgards and the other company pages cited). opened is given only where a page states it (Corpus Christi Liquefaction, 2018).

COORDINATES. US Census Bureau geocoder (batch, Public_AR_Current) for the filed street address, used only when the house number and street agree; otherwise the ArcGIS World geocoder's point address for the same street address; where neither finds the building (a post office box, a highway, a plant on a federal reservation) the EPA registry's point from the ECHO Exporter extract already on disk, cited by its facility report.

FILLS. Thirteen factories other files already describe are given here again with the newer OSHA figure (the loader keeps the newer headcount): Steel Dynamics Sinton, Howmet Wichita Falls, Tyson Vernon, Blue Bell Brenham, Valmont Brenham, Pilgrim's Lufkin and Nacogdoches, Kohler Brownwood (two filings at one address, added), Georgia-Pacific Camden and Pineland, Graphic Packaging Texarkana, W&W-AFCO San Angelo, LyondellBasell Victoria. Each copies the earlier file's place, products and sources and says the earlier figure.

LEFT OUT ON PURPOSE. Distribution centres that file under a maker's industry code (Coca-Cola Southwest Beverages' DCs in Abilene, Lubbock, Tyler, Odessa, Bryan, Corpus Christi, Wichita Falls, Amarillo); repair and overhaul sites (GE Aerospace engine services McAllen, Pratt & Whitney Canada component repairs Wichita Falls, Rolls-Royce at NAS Kingsville, DynaTen at Bell Amarillo, Raytheon at Biggs Army Airfield); ready-mix, precast and other concrete products (Jobe Materials, Permian Basin Materials, Thomas Redi-Mix, Summit Precast, Texas Concrete Partners and others: NOT_COVERED); asphalt paving (Longview Asphalt); Blue Origin's West Texas launch site at Van Horn (587 in 2025), where New Shepard is launched and engines are tested but which no page read says builds anything; Helen of Troy, which designs and sells products made by others and has no factory in El Paso (its old headquarters at 1 Helen of Troy Plaza is now Eaton's plant, already in the data); Smallwood (Longview), whose filing is a management company and whose products are not stated.
